title: Three Nights and One Short Chart
subtitle: 健康医疗 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 健康医疗（人与自我·生活与健康）
meta: 主题语境：健康医疗（人与自我·生活与健康）　|　核心词汇：fever　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fever 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the doctor ① treated a fever that no nurse in the ward would have named, and he said the treating was the whole of the night. The ② fever, meaning the temperature itself and not the illness, ran three nights and stayed unwritten in the book; a fever, he said, is the only thing in a ward that is judged by how long it is left unwritten.

Every ③ fever in that ward had the same short chart beside it, and the ④ fever at the far bed, meaning the one they kept for the child and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A fever, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; the doctor said the naming is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the fever was the whole of the matter, meaning the excitement and not the temperature. The ⑥ fever, meaning the excitement and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody writes down; fever, he said, is either something you treat or the only word that means both a temperature and an excitement. He said the excitement is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ fever had become a line in a chart, and the chart had become an argument about the short night. The ⑧ fever of the whole thing, the doctor wrote in March, was one ward and three nights of naming; fever, he said, is either the one at the far bed or the reason you learned to name. He said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ fever I remember is the one written in the chart, which closed in 1972 and is still described as the quietest in the ward. A ⑩ fever, my mother said in 1974, is the only one that improves by being named; every fever, she said, is an excitement that has agreed to look like a temperature. She said the excitement was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 发烧；发热（指病房里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 发烧（指那一个本身，与疾病相对）
C. 固定搭配：treat a fever 治一场发烧
D. n. 发烧（指留给孩子的那一个）
E. n. 发烧（抽象总称，指一间病房的发热之事）
F. n. 发烧（指病历图表上写到、被命名的那一个）
G. n. 狂热；激动（指一件事里人人都等却无人写下的那样东西）
H. n. 狂热（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人写下的那样东西）

items.q: treated a fever that no nurse in the ward would have named
The fever, meaning the temperature itself and not the illness
the fever at the far bed
the fever was the whole of the matter
the fever had become a line in a chart
The fever of the whole thing
A fever, my mother said in 1974

answers.why: treat a fever 意为“治一场发烧”，1963 年医生治了一场病房里没有一位护士肯说破的发烧。
fever 意为“发烧”，指那一个本身而不是疾病，它持续了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被写下。
fever 意为“发烧”，指病房里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一张短短的病历表。
fever 意为“发烧”，指留给孩子的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
fever 意为“狂热、激动”，指一件事里人人都等却无人写下的那样东西，叔叔说这场激动就是那件事的全部。
fever 意为“狂热”，指人人都等却无人写下的那样东西而不是那一场发烧，是事情里人人都等、却无人写下的东西。
fever 意为“发烧”，指病历图表上写到、被命名的那一个，到 1970 年这一个成了图表里的一行。
fever 意为“发烧”，医生三月写道，整件事的发热之事是一间病房和三个夜晚的说破。
fever 意为“发烧”，我记得的是图表里写下的那一个，1972 年结束了，至今仍被说成病房里最安静的一个。
fever 为抽象总称，母亲 1974 年说，一场发烧是唯一会因为被好好说破而变得更好的东西。
